title: The Letter of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In 1945, Oscar Blackwood, a young woman passing as an apprentice under her late father's clockmaker name, is summoned to Nagasaki's harbor district to repair the observatory's master clock. When the army requisitions the port and seizes the harbor ledger containing the names of foreign residents, smugglers, and townsfolk who sheltered them, Oscar realizes the record will be rewritten to erase the community that raised her. Racing against the victors' historians and a sympathetic but compromised army archivist, she copies, hides, and finally testifies to the ledger's truth, at the cost of her father's name and her own safety. The novel ends with the master clock restored and running, and the true ledger deposited with a neutral consul, its names preserved even as the town that knew them disappears into history.
about_author: Juniper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port records across East Asia before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the people who keep records — and the people the records forget.

chapters.title: The Clock That Keeps Everyone's Time
chapters.summary: Oscar Blackwood, third-person POV, arrives in Nagasaki's harbor district with her father's tools and a forged letter of apprenticeship. The observatory's master clock is failing, and the town's whistles, tides, and shifts depend on it. Beat: cautious belonging — she is a stranger measuring herself against a community that runs on shared time.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: The harbormaster's clerk, Mr. Ito, shows Oscar the harbor ledger to verify her credentials, and she glimpses names — foreign residents, smugglers, families who sheltered castaways — that the official histories never mention. POV: Oscar. Beat: wonder and unease; she begins to understand the ledger is the town's true memory.

chapters.title: An Apprentice of Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Oscar's POV: her father's death, her decision to take his name and trade, and the fear of being unmasked as a woman in a man's workshop. Beat: the price of survival already paid once, establishing the pattern she must break by the end.

chapters.title: The Requisition Order
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive at the harbor and post a requisition order claiming the port, the warehouses, and all records within. POV alternates between Oscar and Lieutenant Hayashi, the archivist ordered to inventory the town's papers. Beat: dread — the ledger is now state property, and state property gets rewritten.

chapters.title: What the Army Wants With Paper
chapters.summary: Hayashi begins cataloguing documents with meticulous, almost reverent care, while Oscar repairs the clock under the soldiers' watchful eyes. POV: Oscar, watching Hayashi work. Beat: wary fascination — she recognizes in him a fellow keeper of time, which makes him more dangerous, not less.

chapters.title: The Whistler's Daughter
chapters.summary: Oscar befriends Sanae, daughter of the harbor whistler, whose father's name appears in the ledger beside a sealed incident from decades ago. POV: Sanae. Beat: the personal stakes surface — Sanae's family history is one of the entries the army's version will erase.

chapters.title: A Copy Made by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Oscar begins secretly copying the ledger's most incriminating pages at night in the clock tower, using the gear-room's hidden light. POV: Oscar. Beat: the point of no return — loyalty to the town now requires betraying the requisition.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Doubt
chapters.summary: Hayashi discovers a discrepancy between the ledger and the official file he is assembling, and quietly withholds the page rather than destroy it. POV: Hayashi. Beat: conscience stirring — the antagonist's humanity complicates the conflict.

chapters.title: Tides and Deadlines
chapters.summary: The army announces the ledger will be sealed and shipped to the capital within three weeks, where historians will produce the official account. POV: Oscar. Beat: the clock starts ticking in earnest; the repair of the master clock and the rescue of the ledger become one race.

chapters.title: What Ito Knew
chapters.summary: The old clerk Ito confesses to Oscar that he once falsified an entry to protect Sanae's father, and fears the army audit will uncover it. POV: Ito. Beat: guilt and loyalty in collision — the town's keepers of truth are also its keepers of merciful lies.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: A senior auditor arrives unannounced; Oscar hides the copied pages inside the master clock's case as soldiers search the tower. POV: Oscar. Beat: terror and improvisation — the clock that keeps the town's time now keeps its secrets.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Hayashi, suspecting what Oscar has done, offers to look away — if she gives him the one page naming a man he is ordered to find. POV: Hayashi. Beat: moral bargaining; both keepers of records must decide what a name is worth.

chapters.title: The Whistle Stops
chapters.summary: The harbor whistle falls silent when its mechanism is requisitioned for scrap, and the town's rhythm breaks; Sanae's father is detained for questioning. POV: Sanae. Beat: grief and anger — the cost of survival is being paid in public now.

chapters.title: The Consul's Door
chapters.summary: Oscar approaches a neutral consul's office about depositing the true ledger, and learns the consul will only accept it from someone with standing — a name, a testimony, a risk. POV: Oscar. Beat: the trap of anonymity; to save the record she must put herself on it.

chapters.title: Hayashi's Own Ledger
chapters.summary: Hayashi reveals, in a tense night conversation in the archive, that his family was erased from a registry years ago, and that he became an archivist to make records honest. POV: Hayashi. Beat: the antagonist becomes an ally of conscience — but a divided one.

chapters.title: The Night the Pages Vanished
chapters.summary: Someone steals the original ledger's key pages; suspicion falls on Oscar, and Ito covers for her at terrible cost. POV: Ito. Beat: betrayal and sacrifice — the community closes ranks around its false apprentice.

chapters.title: Running the Mechanism
chapters.summary: Oscar completes the master clock's repair while planning the ledger's escape aboard a neutral mail steamer, using the clock's chimes to signal the handoff. POV: Oscar. Beat: convergence — craft, courage, and timing fuse into a single plan.

chapters.title: The Handoff at the Pier
chapters.summary: The exchange goes wrong; Sanae is caught carrying the pages, and Hayashi must choose between his orders and his conscience in front of the auditor. POV: Sanae, shifting to Hayashi. Beat: the climax's first blow — loyalty tested in the open.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Hayashi formally enters Oscar's copied pages into the record as verified testimony, burning his career to make the truth official; Oscar, unmasked as a woman, claims her father's work under her own name. POV: Oscar. Beat: the climax — truth on the record, identity claimed, price paid.

chapters.title: What the Victors Write
chapters.summary: The official history is published and gets much wrong — but the consul's deposited ledger survives as a quiet contradiction no one can destroy. POV: Oscar, reading both accounts. Beat: bitter victory; history is contested, never finished.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: On the wharf, the freed townsfolk gather while Sanae reads the ledger's names aloud, restoring the erased to memory. POV: Sanae. Beat: communal healing — belonging reclaimed not by papers but by voice.

chapters.title: The Clock Keeps Time Still
chapters.summary: Years later, Oscar, now a clockmaker under her own name, winds the master clock and adds one final entry to the ledger: her own. POV: Oscar. Beat: resolution — she stopped believing history happens to other people, and wrote herself into it.
